figures.finding: Samoa reported in 2005 that its laws counted minority to twenty-one: the Acts Interpretation Act 1974 makes a minor anyone under twenty-one, the Infants Ordinance 1961 an infant anyone under twenty-one (and a child one under sixteen), and the Electoral Act 1963 an adult one over twenty-one.
figures.applies: Samoa; the State's 2005 report. Later reform (the Infants Ordinance's review was recommended) wasn't established.

sources.said: The ‘Acts Interpretation Act 1974’ states that a ‘minor’ is any person under the age of 21 years.
Under the ‘Infants Ordinance 1961’ a ‘child’ means any infant under the age of 16 years; while an ‘infant’ is any person under the age of 21 years.
